en: "You'd best go on home nice and quiet, yuh."{w}
note: Yeti's -do- verbal tic rendered as a drawled 'yuh' tag; used for both yetis (gatekeeper and storekeeper).

en:
There's a fire alarm.{w}Hitting it with something like {11:0001:0001}
might set it off.{w}
note: {11:0001:0001} = spell name insert (presumably a fire spell, see 2861). | Editorial: "Firing off ... set it off" echoed; reworded.

en: Who will cast it?

That caster hasn't learned
{11:0001:0001}.{w}
note: Subject restored as 'that caster' (the member picked in 2857; no name insert in the row).

en: That caster has used up their spell power.{w}
note: Subject restored as in 2858.

en:
It was only a small flame, but it was
enough to get the fire alarm riled up!{w}
note: Source personifies the alarm (okoraseru = make angry); kept as 'riled up'.

en:
Suddenly everything around you was in an uproar,
and you hurriedly made yourselves scarce.{w}

The fire alarm keeps blaring
its loud fire warning.{w}You'd better get away from here, and fast.{w}
"...Geez, who the heck pulled this prank!!"{w}
"Sheesh, yuh...{w}Good thing it wasn't a real fire, yuh."{w}
"That really ticks me off!{w}Pranks like this are NOT okay, y'hear!"{w}
General Winter
"Miyuki... where have you gone...{w}I could not make your mother happy.{w}I want you, at least, to be happy..."{w}{p}"Why can you not understand my heart...{w}Miyuki... oh, Miyuki...!!"{w}
A fierce blizzard arose, and you were blown away.{w}
"Quit this foolishness, Pa!{w}I found myself a sweetheart down in the village, don't you see!?"{w}
note: Miyuki drops her polite register (slice 046) and speaks rustic, Edo-ish talk to her father: ottsuan/okkasan = 'Pa'/'Ma'. sato = the (human) village, as opposed to the spirits' realm. | Editorial: "you know!?" read flat; "don't you see!?" keeps the indignant !?.

en:
"No... I will not have it, Miyuki...!{w}Some passing stranger like that and a spirit
such as you could never understand each other!!"{w}

"So what if we can't understand each other?
Isn't it enough that the love is there!?"{w}
"You are still young.{w}I will find you a fine husband, mark my words!{w}Hold your tongue and stay where you are!!"{w}
"That's cruel... That's just too much, Pa...{w}Just when I finally had someone who would...{w}accept me for who I am..."{w}
note: Sentence cut at the {w} where the source cuts it.

en: "Oh... you came after me...?{w}...Look, Pa!{w}They braved danger just to come and get me!"{w}
note: First part to the party, rest to her father; the party referred to as 'they'.

en: "So you're the one who led Miyuki astray!{w}Before I lose my temper... Hmm?{w}That thing in your hand..."{w}
You handed General Winter the Wife's Portrait.{w}
note: Key item name 'Wife's Portrait' (okugata no shouzou), see 3101.

en:
"Pa...{w}You and Ma joined your hearts
and pledged yourselves, didn't you?"{w}
note: chigiri wo musubu = pledge (marriage vows); 'pledge' reused in 2943/2944/2960.

en: "That is..."{w}
"Pa, weren't you happy?"{w}
"Ngh... Hnnn..."{w}
"Please understand, Pa.{w}We love each other!!"{w}
"Miyuki..."{w}
At his daughter's words, General Winter lowered the sword he had raised.{w}
"......{w}...Very well. I approve of the two of you."{w}
"Really!?"{w}
"Miyuki, this is my last selfish wish...{w}You understand how a father with a daughter feels, do you not?"{w}
"...All right.{w}Please, you'll win for me, won't you?"{w}
note: Second half addressed to the party.

en: "Son-in-law!{w}Are you worthy of Miyuki or not!?{w}I shall put you to the test!!"{w}
note: mukodono = 'son-in-law' (his word for the suitor); party member's gender not inferred, the word is his. | Editorial: stranded "Whether..." fragment made a spoken question; force kept.

en: You routed General Winter.{w}
"Splendid... splendidly done, son-in-law!{w}A promise is a promise. I shall approve your pledge to Miyuki.{w}Now, which of you loves my daughter the most?"{w}
Who will pledge to Miyuki?

{0A:0003:000F} became engaged to Miyuki.{w}Counting Snow changed into
Counting Snow: First Frost.{w}
note: New item names: kazoe-yuki = 'Counting Snow' (the short blade Miyuki offers in slice 046), kazoe-yuki/hatsushimo = 'Counting Snow: First Frost' (26 chars; check item slot).

en: "Thank you, {0A:0003:000F}...{w}Nothing could make me happier...{w}I'll follow you wherever you go."{w}
"{0A:0003:000F}.{w}I'm counting on you to take good care of Miyuki!!"{w}
"So you're the one who led Miyuki astray!{w}Begone before I lose my temper!!"{w}
"So, is Miyuki keeping well?{w}...Then I have nothing more to say.{w}Take good care of her..."{w}
note: Missing period after the second clause added. | Editorial: "Well? ... doing well" echo removed.

en:
"Miyuki. If you meant to pledge yourself to this one,
you must have given them the Counting Snow, no?"{w}{p}"If they claim to love you!{w}Then why does this one not have the Counting Snow!?{w}The token of the heart that you snow women hold so dear!!"{w}
note: yuki-onna rendered 'snow women'. Suitor kept as 'this one'/'them'. | Editorial: untangled "of the heart of you snow women"; taisetsu = "hold so dear".

en: "Th-that's..."{w}

"Village folk are all talk in the end!{w}The only ones who can make you happy
are those of our own winter kin!!"{w}{p}"Now, I have no further business with you!{w}Begone, before you get yourselves killed!!"{w}
note: fuyu no kenzoku = 'winter kin' (cf. glossary 'Kin of Darkness'). korosarenu uchi ni = before you get killed.

en: Wolf Storekeeper
"Hey, up ahead is the great General Winter's treasure vault."{w}
note: Editorial: "past here is" stiff; sama rendered "the great" as in slice 046 (2846).

en: Yeti Storekeeper
"Go on home before ya get hurt, yuh."{w}
"Hah! Cocky little brats."{w}
"I'm gonna give ya a whuppin', yuh!"{w}
You routed the storekeepers.{w}

Could this be a portrait of General Winter's wife?{w}On the floor lie bundles of neatly sorted love letters.{w}They must have been a devoted couple.{w}{p}Showing this portrait
might win General Winter over.{w}

[Key Item]
You obtained the Wife's Portrait.{w}
note: New key item name 'Wife's Portrait' (okugata = the lady of the house / a noble's wife).

en: Expensive-looking objects and beautiful paintings are crammed in everywhere.{w}
Missionary
"Well, hello there. Nice day for a stroll, isn't it?{w}Is this everyone's first time in the Narmant Trench?{w}How about it, care to hear a little about the trench?"{w}
note: Editorial: doubled greeting "Hey there, hello" smoothed.

en: Hear about the trench?

"This trench is the deepest
in all the Hestrio Continent."{w}{p}"The waters around it are mostly shallows,
so sail through and a shipwreck is guaranteed!{w}That's why sailors go around this trench."{w}{p}"Now, deep, deep within this trench,
at its very bottom, they say the Water Sage,
Lady Shirinmorin, makes her home."{w}{p}"Lately this trench has been rough as rough can be.{w}One theory even goes so far as to say Lady Shirinmorin
is angry... but what's the truth, I wonder?"{w}{p}"Surely, if you were ever to fall into the water,
unless you had an alchemy item like an Air Fruit,
the whirlpools would swallow you and you'd just die."{w}{p}"So, to make sure nothing goes wrong,
you'd all best leave a place like this right away."{w}{p}"Eh? Aren't I in danger too, you ask?{w}Well, you can see what I am.{w}Ha ha haaaaaa!!"{w}
note: Water Sage per glossary. 'their home' kept neutral although the glossary marks Shirinmorin female (the speaker doesn't say). New item name: kuuki no mi = 'Air Fruit'. 'You can see what I am' hints at his nature (he glides off in 2658) without inventing what it is. | Editorial: Shirinmorin-sama = "Lady Shirinmorin" and "her" (female per glossary; as in slices 048/063).

en: The missionary glided off to who knows where.{w}
"Then how about buying a pot?{w}This pot, you see, is a pot that can store up happiness..."{w}
note: Answer to declining the explanation (2655).

en:
"Y-you followed me all the way heeere?!{w}Nooo, I'm so scaaared!!"{w}{p}"I haven't done anything,
so why are you being so mean to me?!{w}Waaah!!"{w}
note: Sedna's panicky voice as in slice 006.

en: Sedna, in tears, heaved an ice floe overhead.{w}And then......{w}
note: furikaburu = raise overhead to swing/throw. Sedna's gender not established; no pronoun used.

en: Sedna Chase Point{w}
note: op096 label; other op096 rows are outcome/death-cause texts ('You got stranded.', 'Suffocated'), so this may be the wipe cause after Sedna's ice floe, or a debug label. oikomi = cornering/chasing. Use unverified.

en: Mermaid Queen

"...What is that child running around
squealing about, I wonder?"{w}
note: 'that child' = Sedna (the neighbouring script 29002), inferred.

en: There's an upward current. Go up to the surface?
Captain Wanelly
"This is... my ship...{w}Our... ship...{w}I won't let... anyone touch iiit..."{w}

Could this be the captain's vengeful ghost?{w}You'd like to free that soul from the bottom
of this cold sea, but...{w}
note: Subject restored as 'you' (party). Captain's gender unknown: 'that soul'.

en: "What're you lot standin' around for!!{w}Don't flinch, fire!!{w}We've still got plenty of shot, so FIIIRE!!"{w}
Suddenly you were grabbed and stuffed into a cannon barrel!!{w}
There's one of the Wanelly's cannons here.{w}
note: Wanelly-gou = 'the Wanelly' (glossary). | Editorial: "Here is" stiff; matches the "There's a ... here." examine lines.

en: Climb into the barrel?

"Damn iiit...{w}I can't lose... I can't lose, I tell ya,
this is my turf... Where's the shot!?"{w}
note: shima = turf (gang-style territory). | Editorial: "Damn iiit ... dammit" doubled; "I tell ya" as in his 2693 voice.
